data.narrative:
Ultra Robotics is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jon Miller Schwartz, Max Friefeld, Chetan Parthiban, and Oliver Ortlieb. The company has raised $3M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader Robotics & Manufacturing comp universe of 10 private peers and 1 public comparable, though narrow peer-stage alignment limits direct benchmarking.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($3M) as a proxy for seed valuation and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $8M. Peer-median benchmarking was not executable; while 10 same-sector companies exist, none met the threshold of three or more datapoints within same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier buckets needed for robust comparison.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6M to $9M, centered on $8M. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient narrow-peer comparables at seed stage in this sector, limiting cross-validation of stage-progression results. The valuation rests principally on standardized step-up mechanics rather than peer triangulation. Additional revenue, product, or market-traction data would improve confidence in narrowing this range.
